# SWTBot

Source: https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot/blob/master/README.md

# SWTBot

SWTBot is a Java API that interacts with SWT by using high-level operations.
It is generally used to write UI tests efficiently since the grain of the API is the same grain as UI operation.
It makes it easier to transform a user scenario into automated tests.

* https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.swtbot

## Documentation & links

https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot/wiki

## Contributing

Pull requests and issues are accepted on GitHub.
See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details, including the required Eclipse Contributor Agreement (ECA) and `Signed-off-by` trailer.

For broader discussions, the project mailing list is `swtbot-dev@eclipse.org`.

---

# SWTBot

Source: https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

# SWTBot

SWTBot is a Java API that interacts with SWT by using high-level operations.
It is generally used to write UI tests efficiently since the grain of the API is the same grain as UI operation.
It makes it easier to transform a user scenario into automated tests.

* https://projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.swtbot

## Documentation & links

https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot/wiki

## Contributing

Pull requests and issues are accepted on GitHub at https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot.

For broader discussions, please use the project mailing list: https://dev.eclipse.org/mailman/listinfo/swtbot-dev.

## Developer resources

The project source code is hosted at https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot.

Issues are tracked on GitHub:

* Browse issues: https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot/issues
* Create a new issue: https://github.com/eclipse-swtbot/org.eclipse.swtbot/issues/new

Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.
Contributions are always welcome.

## Eclipse Contributor Agreement

Before your contribution can be accepted by the project team, contributors must
electronically sign the Eclipse Contributor Agreement (ECA).

* http://www.eclipse.org/legal/ECA.php

Commits that are provided by non-committers must have a `Signed-off-by` field in
the footer indicating that the author is aware of the terms by which the
contribution has been provided to the project.
The non-committer must additionally have an Eclipse Foundation account and must have a signed Eclipse Contributor Agreement (ECA) on file.

For more information, please see the Eclipse Committer Handbook:
https://www.eclipse.org/projects/handbook/#resources-commit

## Contact

Contact the project developers via the project's "dev" list.

* https://dev.eclipse.org/mailman/listinfo/swtbot-dev
